 Elina Svitolina and Karolina Muchova speak out about their crucial WTA Finals clash
 Ewan West 
 11 Nov 2026 3:00 PM 
 Elina Svitolina and Karolina Muchova 
 Elina Svitolina and Karolina Muchova have looked ahead to their crucial round robin clash at the 2026 WTA Finals in Indian Wells.
 The second round of matches in Group 2 at the season-ending championships will take place on Wednesday, with Svitolina facing Muchova before Aryna Sabalenka and Mirra Andreeva meet.
 On Monday, Svitolina suffered a heavy 4-6, 0-6 defeat to Andreeva, while Muchova fell 6-7(2), 5-7 to Sabalenka in a close battle.
 With both players having lost their opening matches in straight sets, the winner of this Svitolina-Muchova contest will significantly improve their chances of qualifying for the semi-finals, while the loser could face elimination. Svitolina holds a 3-1 head-to-head record against Muchova.
 In the third and final set of round robin matches, Svitolina will play Sabalenka, while Muchova will take on Andreeva.
 Speaking to the WTA after losing to Andreeva, Svitolina discussed the challenge of facing Muchova.
 “Yeah, there’s gonna be definitely a different plan for that one,” said the 32-year-old Ukrainian.

 “I played a couple of times, I know a few things that I have to work on tomorrow to be better and also that can work against her. I think it will be important for me to focus on myself, on the execution.
 “And yeah, it’s gonna be a fun match. She’s a tricky player, lots of variety on her game. So yeah, I will try to do my very best to be ready for that.”
 After her defeat to Sabalenka, Muchova was asked about playing Svitolina and Andreeva, with her next opponent unconfirmed at the time.
 “I feel like here, you don’t really pick an opponent you would want (laughs),” said the 30-year-old Czech.
 “Even now, playing the first match against Aryna, world No 2… you have to go here to every match to play your best tennis, your 100%, to really pour it on the court.
 “So, Mirra and Elina are unbelievable players, and it’s gonna be another really, really tough match.”
 Muchova is making her WTA Finals debut, while 2018 champion Svitolina is appearing at the tournament for the fourth time.
